# Phase 5: General coding fluency

*30 minutes daily from week 3* · [Track on the site](https://arubad.github.io/AI_Research_Journey/#p5)

Target: LeetCode Mediums consistently under 25 minutes, with AI off. This is a daily habit, not a phase, because algorithmic patterns leak into ML-coding rounds (top-K heaps are decoding; sliding windows are sliding-window attention; DP is beam search and edit distance). Alisa's two lists are the whole syllabus: [LeetCode 75](https://leetcode.com/studyplan/leetcode-75/) first, then [NeetCode Blind 75](https://neetcode.io/practice/practice/blind75).

| Topic | Reach fluency in | ML tie-in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arrays, strings, hash maps | The base of most problems | Tokenizer merge tables |
| Two pointers / sliding window | Fixed and variable windows | Sliding-window attention, local masks |
| Binary search | Including search on the answer space | Hyperparameter bisection, top-p cutoff |
| Stacks, queues | BFS/DFS traversal patterns | Beam-search frontier |
| Trees | DFS, BFS, LCA; trees disguised as graphs | Parse trees, MCTS-style search |
| Graphs | BFS, DFS, topological sort, Dijkstra | Autograd DAG ordering, pipeline schedules |
| Dynamic programming | 1D and 2D; memo vs tabulation; edit distance, coin change, LCS | Viterbi, CTC, beam search |
| Heaps / priority queues | Top-K problems | Top-k sampling, beam search |
| Sorting | Quick, merge, heap; time and space for each | Length-bucketing batches |

Keep a one-line log per problem (pattern, time, mistake). Every two weeks, redo the five slowest.

Log every problem in `log.csv`; keep solutions in `solutions/`.


Sources: [alisa-roadmap README, Phase 4](https://github.com/soasme/alisa-roadmap) · [Notes on the Industry Job Search, Appendix](https://alisawuffles.github.io/blog/job-search/)
